question_text: According to the Commonwealth of Learning (COL, 2015) definition used in this unit, open and distance learning is characterised by:
option_a: Physical presence of teacher and learner at all times
option_b: Separation of teacher and learner in time and/or space, with multiple media for instruction
option_c: Only written correspondence with no other media
option_d: A single mode of instructional delivery
explanation: COL (2015) defines ODL as a system of teaching and learning characterised by separation of teacher and learner in time and/or space, using multiple media for delivery of instruction.

question_text: Who is credited with the first officially recognised attempt at distance education, teaching shorthand by mail in the 1840s?
explanation: Sir Isaac Pitman taught shorthand by mail starting in the 1840s, considered the first officially recognised attempt at distance education.

question_text: According to Schultz, Schultz and Embry-Riddle (2008), the three developmental stages of distance education are:
explanation: The three-stage development followed in this unit is: correspondence stage, sound and video signal stage, and computer technology stage.

question_text: Which Nigerian university was first to operate the dual mode of open and distance learning at the tertiary level, via its University of the Air (1972)?
explanation: Ahmadu Bello University first employed ODL at the tertiary level, establishing the University of the Air in 1972.

question_text: The National Open University of Nigeria (NOUN) was first established in 1983 but suspended in 1984 by General Muhammad Buhari; it was later re-established in what year?
explanation: NOUN was re-established in 2002 during the tenure of Chief Olusegun Obasanjo, after the original 1983 establishment was suspended in 1984.

question_text: Which former Nigerian president enrolled as a student at NOUN after leaving office, eventually earning a PhD in Christian Theology?
explanation: Chief Olusegun Obasanjo enrolled at NOUN after leaving office, becoming the first doctoral graduate of Christian Theology at NOUN.

question_text: According to statistics cited in this unit, what percentage of qualified Nigerian applicants could not gain admission to conventional universities (per Umar, 2006)?
explanation: Umar (2006) estimated about 80% of qualified prospective students could not gain admission into conventional universities.

question_text: NOUN is described in this unit as the only institution in Nigeria operating which mode of ODL?
explanation: NOUN is the only mono-mode open and distance learning university in Nigeria as of the time of this unit's writing.

question_text: The 1977 National Policy on Education (NPE) is cited in this unit as evidence that Nigeria's ODL development is:
option_b: Rooted in a formal government policy
option_c: Copied entirely from the UK model
explanation: The 1977 NPE anticipated the coming of open and distance learning, showing that Nigeria's ODL development is rooted in policy.

question_text: Which body was established in 2003, in partnership with the Commonwealth of Learning (COL), to support ODL research and capacity building in West Africa?
explanation: The Regional Training and Research Institute for Open and Distance Learning (RETRIDAL) was established in 2003 in partnership with COL.

question_text: The first Open University in the world, established in 1969 in the United Kingdom, is called:
explanation: The Open University was established in 1969 as a public distance learning and research university, one of the biggest in the UK.

question_text: Openness in ODL, per Kanwar (2015), can be discussed in three major areas. Which of the following is one of them?
option_a: Openness as to people, place, and ideas
explanation: Kanwar (2015) discusses openness in three major areas: openness as to people, place, and ideas.

question_text: Who coined the term 'open content' in 1998, referring to educational content that can be reused, revised, remixed, and redistributed without violating copyright?
explanation: David Wiley coined the term 'open content' in 1998; this led to the Open Educational Resources (OER) and MOOCs movements.

question_text: Flexibility in ODL, as discussed in this unit, is examined across which three areas?
explanation: Flexibility can be examined in three areas: place, time, and pace, according to this unit.

question_text: According to research cited in this unit, which disadvantaged groups have gained access to higher education through the accessibility offered by ODL?
explanation: Prisoners and women in purdah are cited as disadvantaged groups who have gained access to higher education through ODL's accessibility.

question_text: How many types of interactivity does this unit identify as characteristic of ODL?
explanation: Four kinds of interactivity are named: learner-to-content, learner-to-instructor, learner-to-learner, and learner-to-technology.

question_text: Which type of interactivity refers to the time a learner spends engaging with textbooks, PowerPoints, and web pages?
explanation: Learner-to-content interactivity refers to time spent with course content, including textbooks, PowerPoint, and web pages (Zimmerman, 2012).

question_text: The learning approach that shifts instructional focus from the teacher to the learner, aiming to improve students' learning rather than mere transmission of information, is called:
explanation: Learner-centred learning shifts the focus of instruction from the teacher to the learner, aiming at improving students' learning and success.

question_text: Which of the following is listed as a component of NOUN's affordability, according to this unit?
explanation: NOUN runs flexible payment plans, allowing students to pay compulsory fees at once and defer course/examination fee payment, as part of its affordability.

question_text: The mixed-media courseware feature of ODL, as described in this unit, includes which of the following media types?
option_b: Print, radio, television, audio, video, computer-based instruction, and telecommunications
explanation: Mixed-media courseware includes print, radio, television broadcast, audio, video, computer-based instruction, and telecommunications.

question_text: According to this unit, separation of teacher and learner occurs in which two planes?
explanation: Separation of teacher and learner occurs in two planes: place (physical distance) and time (including different time zones or asynchronous study times).

question_text: According to this unit, the role of the ODL teacher has shifted from being the 'dispenser of information' to being described (by Bull, 2013) as more like:
explanation: Bull (2013) describes the online teacher's role as similar to a 'tour guide', directing and redirecting learners' attention toward key concepts.

question_text: According to a study cited at the Lagos Study Centre (Adewale, 2014), what was the gender distribution of NOUN respondents?
explanation: Adewale (2014) found 40% of respondents at Lagos Study Centre were male, while 60% were female.

question_text: According to the age distribution data cited in this unit, which age range represented the largest percentage of NOUN students?
explanation: The 21-30 age range represented 40% of respondents, the largest single age group in the cited data.

question_text: Which of the following is listed as a characteristic quality expected of an ODL learner in this unit?
option_d: Preference for isolation over all collaboration
explanation: Discipline (self-discipline, self-monitoring, self-initiative, self-management) is listed as a key quality expected of a successful ODL learner.

question_text: Learning environment, as defined by Warger and Dobbin (2009) in this unit, encompasses which of the following?
option_b: Learning resources, technology, teaching methods, and human/cultural dimensions
explanation: Warger and Dobbin (2009) define learning environment as encompassing learning resources and technology, teaching modes, and human/cultural dimensions.

question_text: The three roles of the teacher in ODL identified in this unit are:
option_b: Creator/manager of learning environment, instructor, facilitator
explanation: The three major roles of the ODL teacher discussed are: creator and manager of learning environment, instructor, and facilitator.

question_text: According to Cranton (1989), who did open and distance learning students traditionally consist of, and how has this changed?
option_a: Mostly adult students traditionally, now increasingly young adults
option_c: Always young adults, unchanged over time
option_d: Mostly retirees, now mostly working professionals
explanation: Cranton (1989) suggested ODL students were traditionally mostly adults, but this unit notes young adults aged 16-31 now form the majority.

question_text: According to this unit, is the role of the teacher in ODL fixed and identical to that of a conventional classroom teacher?
option_b: No -- the teacher's role is changing, moving away from being the sole 'dispenser of information'
option_c: The teacher has no role at all in ODL
option_d: Only the learner has a role, never the teacher
explanation: The teacher's role is changing; the teacher is no longer the sole 'dispenser of information' as in traditional education (O'Neil, 2006).

question_text: According to the employment status data cited in this unit, what percentage of NOUN students in the study were classified as employed?
explanation: The cited study showed 45.2% of students were employed, 30% unemployed, and 24.8% self-employed.

question_text: Reflective skill, as defined by Dabbagh (2007) in this unit, is the ability to:
option_a: Ignore one's own learning process entirely
option_b: Apply frequent and substantive consideration and assessment of one's own learning process and products
option_c: Only reflect on others' work, never one's own
option_d: Avoid keeping any record of learning
explanation: Dabbagh (2007) defines reflective skills as the ability to apply frequent and substantive consideration and assessment of one's own learning process and products.
